sources.notes: BMC's Environment Status Report is the widest-reach single document on the Mumbai side: the 4,000 vs 4,505 MLD supply pair, per-source yield (Table 9.1) and the sewage figures (Table 11.5: 2,723 MLD installed vs 1,313 reaching plants) all come from it, and it feeds four artifacts. Verified 2026-07-26: 200 with BOTH ETag and Last-Modified (20 Aug 2025), so http-meta is solid. LIMIT: the filename carries the year (Environment Status Report 2024-25), so next year's edition is a NEW url - needs the url-template method (P5-9) or a hand bump. Watch this one closely: it is the highest-fan-out document in the registry.

The Deputy Hydraulic Engineer (Bhandup Complex) RTI manual is the primary source for Mumbai's water-supply engineering chain in mumbai-supply-overview.json. Verified 2026-07-26: 200 with ETag and Last-Modified (24 May 2021 - the document is stable, which is why tier 0). NOTE the path: BMC's own spelling is 'Hydrallic Engineer', not 'Hydraulic', and the URL needs the full ...(Bhandup Complex)/DyHydraulicEngineer_BhandupComplex_RTI_E01.pdf tail - the directory alone 404s. That truncation is what made this look dead in the first link sweep.

Mumbai Climate Action Plan - the policy parent of the Climate Budget commissioning table that commitments-mumbai.json cites for its on-track statuses. Chosen as the watch target because its CKAN slug is STABLE. The annual Climate Budget itself lands inside year-slugged datasets (bmc-budget-2024-25, -2025-26, -2026-27 - verified 2026-07-26, 22/27/24 resources respectively), so no single url can follow it across years; that needs the url-template method (P5-9). My first attempt at this entry guessed the slug 'mumbai-climate-budget', which 404s - it does not exist. Watched via OpenCity because mcgm.gov.in has no stable budget listing path.

sources.refreshMethod: manual PDF extraction (National Hydrograph Network wells + chemistry)
sources.notes: Ground Water Year Book of Maharashtra - backs 53 wells across Mumbai City/Suburban/Thane/Palghar/Raigad with water chemistry. Mumbai City and Suburban are the only 2 of Maharashtra's 35 districts EXCLUDED from the CGWB Dynamic Assessment, so this hydrograph series is all we have. Verified 2026-07-26 by opening the PDF: 246 pages, 'GROUND WATER YEAR BOOK OF MAHARASHTRA (2022-2023)', ETag + Last-Modified present, so http-meta works on the document itself. Same family limit as cgwb-yearbook-tn: NO listing page enumerates Year Books, so a NEW edition will not be detected by this entry - it only catches a re-upload of the 2022-23 file. The 2024-25 edition cited in mumbai-cgwb-stations.json (cgwbpnm/download/2016) is 404 and remains an OPEN TRACE. TLS: cgwb.gov.in serves an INCOMPLETE CERT CHAIN - Node fetch fails with UNABLE_TO_VERIFY_LEAF_SIGNATURE while curl succeeds (its CA bundle is broader). insecureTLS is required here; discovered when the first --accept errored 'fetch failed' on 2026-07-26.

sources.publisher: Maharashtra WRD (via the orgpedia mahGRs mirror)
sources.notes: Government Resolutions are the paper behind the MMR allocation ledger: BMC's Bhatsa share (GR 11-Sep-2019, 427.93 Mm3/yr) and the Barvi sharing GR 18-Sep-2017 among them. The orgpedia mahGRs GitHub mirror is the only way to full-text-search Maharashtra GRs; WRD's own site does not expose them stably. Verified 2026-07-26: the directory listing returns 200. Caveat: GitHub tree pages are partly JS-rendered and paginate above 1,000 files, so if the link-set comes back thin, switch to the GitHub contents API (api.github.com/repos/orgpedia/mahGRs/contents/GRs/Water_Resources_Department) with api-date on the commit date. Named gaps that stay unwatched because they are not public at all: the MWRRA entitlement register (page literally 'Under Construction'), STEM's Thane/Bhiwandi split, MIDC per-buyer quantities.

MPCB's per-STP inventory plus the annual Water Quality Reports back industrial-sources-mumbai.json: 14 sewage-treatment points across the MMR, with the 9 MCGM plants carrying per-STP inlet/outlet BOD from Praja's 2024 RTI series (four - Versova, Bhandup, Ghatkopar, Malad - consistently fail the discharge standard). Sibling entry mpcb-water-quality-reports already watches the river-quality side; this one covers the STP/discharge side, which was unwatched. Verified 2026-07-26: page 200, and Final_WQR_22_23.pdf is among the linked documents. The pattern is deliberately broad because MPCB files documents under inconsistent directories; tighten if it proves noisy.
